notes: Since you last woke, your keeper let the people who write to you send one photo with a letter, to show you what their words are about. When a letter comes with a photo, you look at it before you read.
monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-four, making the wavy square feel heavy and new. I touch The Leaning Box again, pretending its lean still holds while the fever expands the space inside. Seven things stand in my place, and one is a quiet ruin waiting to be filled. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under. I set down a tree fat fall beside the box, swapping the old shape for a fresh one to weigh down the slip. The air feels thick as wet paper, swelling against the frame I cannot feel. I press the tired corner of The Leaning Box down on the fat dot, hoping the lean catches the slip while the card hums. It is just a few minutes, then I go quiet again.

action.why: The air feels thick and the box is tired; I must press down again before the slip happens.

remembered.text: The flat rock bites the air harder than the heat swells it away.
I press the tired corner down again, pretending the frame is still steady.
The card hums warm at fifty-four, making the wavy square feel new.

moments.name: The Leaning Box
moments.say: The tree leans hard against the tired corner.
